What Apple Background Sounds is for end users — not engineering

On iPhone and iPad, Apple Background Sounds is an Accessibility feature that plays continuous ambient audio — rain, ocean, stream, and other built-in loops — to mask distracting noise and support focus or calm. Buyers find it in Settings → Accessibility → Audio & Visual → Background Sounds. For App Store marketing, that story lives in screenshot galleries and description copy when your app complements or extends that experience:

  • Background Sounds picker — onboarding or settings screens that let users choose rain, ocean, stream, or other ambient loops
  • Focus and calm soundscapes — marketing frames that show continuous ambient audio for study, sleep, meditation, or noise masking
  • Rain, ocean, and stream noise — gallery art naming specific sound types buyers recognize from Apple's built-in set or your custom library
  • Volume and mix controls — in-app sliders or presets when your US listing shows adjustable ambient levels beside soundscape thumbnails
  • 背景声音 / 背景音 / 环境背景音 — zh-Hans storefront terms Chinese buyers search when looking for calm ambient audio apps, not speech captions or alert notifications

Those are product-page stories — how you describe ambient soundscape value to China buyers in zh-Hans. They are separate from AVAudioEngine implementation, loop file encoding, or configuring Apple's system Background Sounds toggle in iOS Settings.
